title: An interoceptive model of energy allostasis linking metabolic and mental health
identity_check: File opens with 'An interoceptive model of energy allostasis linking metabolic and mental health', Mehrhof S. Z., Fleming H., Nord C. L. (Review, Sci Adv), DOI 10.1126/sciadv.ady4356 -> matches verified two-channel metadata (overlap 1.0, year 2025).
mapping_note: Paper's own words -> our K-family: 'predicts future needs and prepares to satisfy them before they arise ... allostasis: anticipatory regulation' -> K5 delay/memory (the paper's temporal vocabulary is 'timescales'/'anticipation', not 'delay'); 'prediction errors underpin learning ... the internal model is recalibrated' and 'feeding back into the cycle' -> K6 feedback; 'learning from prediction errors is metabolically costly ... must estimate their precision to determine whether they are worth integrating' -> K11 resource constraint (paper says 'cost'/'energy cost', never 'resource constraint'); 'the model may become "stuck" in a state that was adaptive in a previous context but maladaptive in the present' -> K7 hysteresis (candidate, not coded for the 3-entry cap).
description_scope: Action judged under the descriptions 'eat / seek a food reward' and 'expend effort (physical activity)': the paper's claim is that interoceptive prediction sets BOTH, in opposite directions depending on the predicted energy state, so the record-level direction is only meaningful relative to one of these descriptions (02 2.1-1). Value/valuation language alone ('energy scarcity', 'reward sensitivity') is not treated as the claim; the claim is about which behavior is initiated or withdrawn.
motion_source: L3/L4 - humoral and vagal metabolic signals (ghrelin, insulin, leptin, immune signals) integrated into a predictive internal model in NTS/hippocampus/hypothalamus/insula/BLA, which then drives top-down regulation and effort-based decisions.

mechanism.claim: Allostasis moves control of action ahead of the bodily signal: rather than waiting for an imbalance, the brain predicts future needs and initiates regulatory action before they arise - so what brings the organism to act is a remembered/predicted state, not the present one (direction of the action depends on the predicted content).
mechanism.quote: Hence, rather than waiting for an imbalance to occur, the brain predicts future needs and prepares to satisfy them before they arise ( 19 , 22 , 181 – 184 ). This predictive regulation of future physiological needs is termed allostasis: anticipatory regulation of bodily state.

mechanism.claim: The model is kept in sync by a closed comparison loop: top-down predictions are compared with bottom-up signals, the discrepancy (prediction error) recalibrates the model, and the loop is explicitly described as a self-maintaining cycle between cognition, behavior and metabolism; the loop itself is polarity-free - it stabilizes whatever set-point it has been trained on.
mechanism.quote: These top-down predictions are compared to the bottom-up signals; a discrepancy between the two leads to a prediction error. Prediction errors underpin learning: To minimize the error signals, the internal model is recalibrated, allowing more accurate future predictions.

mechanism.claim: Updating is energetically expensive, so the brain must estimate the precision of a prediction error to decide whether it is worth integrating; low-precision errors are discounted or ignored, producing failure to learn, a model increasingly out of sync with reality, and the amotivational/inattentive behavior the paper links to depression (no new engagement means no errors at all, which entrenches the model).
mechanism.quote: However, learning from prediction errors is metabolically costly; it necessitates the encoding and consolidation of information, brain computations associated with an energy cost ( 22 , 208 , 209 ). Because of this, the brain must estimate their precision to determine whether they are worth integrating.

event_grammar: [MOTION] bottom-up metabolic signals (gut hormones, vagal stretch, immune) enter the internal model --> [GATE] precision-weighted prediction error decides whether anything is learned, under an energy-cost constraint --> [ACTION/INACTION] prospective regulation: eating/foraging initiated before need, or effort and activity withdrawn when predicted scarcity raises effort costs --> [OUTCOME] energy allostasis maintained, or metabolic plus psychiatric comorbidity --> [FEEDBACK] behavior changes metabolism, which changes the signals the model predicts from (vicious/virtuous closed loop)

anchor_concordance.reason: Both records make K5 primary, but the anchor's delayed-feedback mechanism binds an outcome to produce REFUSAL of the paired food (D-), whereas this paper's allostasis uses prediction to INITIATE regulation ahead of the signal (coded D+ for its primary entry); the paper's own D- branch (effort withdrawal, apathy) sits in the K11/prediction-failure sections.

notes: Science Advances conceptual review: no new data; the authors mark their own claims as proposals ('we propose', 'which we hypothesize'), so the record is PAPER_CLAIM at theoretical level and must not be escalated to SUPPORTED_MECHANISM. Its postoral-reinforcement passage restates the anchor's amygdalar reactivation account (their ref 200) and is therefore not independent evidence. Two strong candidates were dropped under the 3-entry cap: K2 (the brain 'inhibiting the activity of hunger neurons in response to food-predicting cues, before actual consumption') and K7 (the model 'stuck' in a previously adaptive state - hysteresis). Formal/quantitative claims are absent: precision-weighting is stated as a mathematical intuition (Fig. 3), so no L0 quantitative coding was made. Per 07-registry C-03, K5 and K6 are hung separately.
